rv.q: The show skips so rapidly and lightly over so much ground that it ends up being both difficult to follow and to connect with emotionally.
This oddly named play is a love story as well as the drama of a serious health risk faced by many women.
But in Greenblatt’s play, a few too many self-conscious devices and a few too many on-the-nose metaphors around cloth and plants add distance from the emotional journey of the play.
However, once produced, the blend of music, dance, monologues and dream-like scenes come across as rather heavy handed.
Haley Basil, who does a phenomenal job acting

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this impressionistic blend of music, movement, and personal illness narrative. Critics praise its atmospheric staging and important BRCA awareness message, but find the storytelling uneven.
